title: ICE Killings are Acts of Terrorism
author: Mitchell Zimmerman
content:
![](https://www.counterpunch.org/wp-
content/uploads/2026/01/Screenshot-2026-01-15-at-4.41.52-PM-680x508.png)

Photograph by Nathaniel St. Clair

In less than one week, ICE agents killed twice.

Neither victim was the man they were looking for. And each time their excuses
made no sense. But the killings served a purpose: terrorizing immigrant
communities, in pursuit of Trump’s white nationalist agenda.

On July 7 in Houston, masked ICE agents who did not identify themselves
stopped and [shot to death Lorenzo Salgado
Araujo](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/07/09/us/witnesses-houston-ice-
shooting.html), a 52 year old Mexican national and father of three. Araujo had
lived in the United States for 35 years and had applied to obtain legal
status. He was on his way to work in construction.

Using its by-now familiar excuse, Homeland Security officials [claimed that
Araujo rammed an ICE
vehicle](https://www.theguardian.com/commentisfree/2026/jul/14/lorenzo-
salgado-araujo-ice) and tried to run down ICE agents by “weaponizing” his van.
The claim was [disputed by
witnesses](https://www.theguardian.com/commentisfree/2026/jul/14/lorenzo-
salgado-araujo-ice), is inconsistent with the [video
evidence](https://www.youtube.com/shorts/o4aLnIUxj5Y), and makes no sense.

Araujo had no criminal record. Why would this law-abiding, middle-aged family
man ram an ICE vehicle and try to kill ICE agents?

Six days later, in Biddeford, Maine, ICE killed again. This time they killed
Johan Sebastian Guerrero, a [26-year-old Colombian man who was authorized to
work](https://abcnews.com/US/ice-agent-involved-shooting-maine-
authorities/story?id=134714502) in the United States.

Again, ICE claimed that Guerrero tried to run down the ICE agent. Again, no
evidence supported the excuse. Twelve hours later Homeland Security abandoned
the “weaponized” vehicle claim and tried another story: The ICE agent,
“[fearing for public safety](https://www.cnn.com/2026/07/13/us/live-
news/maine-ice-shooting-houston-minnesota?post-id=cmrjtdyds000j3b6ro2ucew19),”
shot Guerrero because he “attempted to flee the scene.”

Under Homeland Security’s account, an unmarked ICE vehicle driven by an
unknown masked man attempts to stop a vehicle, the driver (who was not their
intended target) tries to escape, and the agent fires. They claim,
essentially, that failing to stop ([if that actually even
happened](https://www.cnn.com/2026/07/14/us/video/ice-shooting-maine-witness-
digvid-vrtc)) amounts to “fleeing the scene” — and requires deadly force.

[Johan Sebastian Guerrero](https://www.pressherald.com/2026/07/14/who-is-joan-
sebastian-guerrero-the-man-killed-by-ice-in-biddeford/) was working legally at
two jobs, as a cleaner and a food delivery driver. He had a wife and a three-
year-old daughter. Who can claim he was so dangerous he had to be killed?

Since Trump returned to the White House, ICE agents have killed at least [10
times](https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/jul/09/ice-immigration-
shooting-deaths-trump), including Renee Good and Alex Pretti, as of this
writing.

ICE agents [routinely shoot](https://www.wsj.com/us-news/videos-show-how-ice-
vehicle-stops-can-escalate-to-shootings-caf17601) at people in vehicles, even
though [official U.S. government
policy](https://www.justice.gov/jm/1-16000-department-justice-policy-use-
force#:~:text=Firearms%20may%20not,of%20deadly%20force.) warns against the
practice and says law enforcement officers should “move out of the path of the
vehicle” rather than shoot. In addition, at least 49 people have [died in ICE
custody](https://nipnlg.org/news/mourning-those-who-have-died-ice-custody) so
far in Trump’s second term — a number that will only climb.

Brutality and [violence](https://americanoversight.org/newsletter/ice-
violence-is-up-under-trump-and-dhs-has-known-for-nearly-a-year/) are [routine
feature](https://www.americanimmigrationcouncil.org/fact-sheet/ice-cbp-legal-
analysis/)s of ICE operations, yet no ICE agent has been held responsible. In
Trump’s war against immigrants, ICE agents know they may slay with impunity.

Donald Trump’s campaign of demonization and vilification sets the stage. Trump
calls immigrants “[animals](https://www.reuters.com/world/us/trump-expected-
highlight-murder-michigan-woman-immigration-speech-2024-04-02/)” and “[not
human](https://www.reuters.com/world/us/trump-expected-highlight-murder-
michigan-woman-immigration-speech-2024-04-02/),” likening them to [criminals
or escaped mental
patients](https://www.themarshallproject.org/2024/10/21/fact-
check-12000-trump-statements-
immigrants/emptying_prisons_jails_mental_institutions#emptying_prisons_jails_mental_institutions).
He calls them “vermin” who “infest our country,” and he embraces the Nazi
theme that a despised group is “[poisoning the blood of our
country](https://www.washingtonpost.com/politics/2023/12/22/trump-campaign-
immigrants-mass-deportations/).”

The unrestrained brutality of ICE is a reign of terror. Killing without cause
is not a problem for the Department of Homeland Security; it is a feature.
ICE’s indiscriminate violence conveys that nonwhite immigrants, lawful or
otherwise, have no place in Trump’s America.

There is little point in considering DHS’s pretexts for killing on a case-by-
case basis. ICE’s abuse of immigrants is not the result of individual misdeeds
— it is policy. ICE cannot be reformed because its purpose is not enforcing
the law. It is terrorism for a white supremacist vision of America.

Those who reject Trump’s vision, who insist on the humanity of our neighbors,
who still believe we must welcome to America’s shores those yearning to
breathe free, must stand up and say No.
